title: gRPC length-prefixed message frame
summary: gRPC messages on the wire are framed with a 5-byte prefix: 1 byte compression flag (0 = uncompressed, 1 = compressed) followed by a 4-byte big-endian message length, then the (possibly compressed) serialized protobuf message. Used over HTTP/2 DATA frames.

ext.summary: gRPC messages on the wire are framed with a 5-byte prefix: 1 byte compression flag (0 = uncompressed, 1 = compressed) followed by a 4-byte big-endian message length, then the (possibly compressed) serialized protobuf message. Used over HTTP/2 DATA frames.

structure.meaning: 0 = message is not compressed, 1 = message is compressed (per grpc-encoding header).
Length of the message payload in bytes (big-endian, max 2^32-1, default limit 4 MiB).
Serialized protobuf (or other codec) bytes; compressed if flag = 1.

ext.example_decoded: Uncompressed frame, 10-byte payload 'Hello gRPC' (protobuf string field)
notes: gRPC uses HTTP/2 streams: one stream per RPC call.
Trailers (HTTP/2 HEADERS with END_STREAM) carry the status code (grpc-status) and message.
Default max message size is 4 MiB (grpc.max_receive_message_length).
Streaming RPCs send multiple length-prefixed messages on the same stream.
The compression flag refers to per-message compression (gzip), distinct from HTTP/2 header compression (HPACK).
